title: Pretérito Mais-que-Perfeito Composto / Compound Pluperfect
bridge: In Spanish, the past of the past is expressed with the pluperfect (había + past participle). In Portuguese, there is an equivalent compound form: tinha + past participle. But be careful: Portuguese also has a simple pluperfect (e.g., 'falara') which in Spanish sounds like the imperfect subjunctive ('hablara'). For B1 level, we focus on the compound form, which is the most commonly used in everyday speech. Remember that in Portuguese, the auxiliary verb is 'ter' (not 'haber'), and the past participle can vary in gender and number in some constructions.
rule: The compound pluperfect is formed with the imperfect indicative of the verb 'ter' (tinha, tinhas, tinha, tínhamos, tínheis, tinham) followed by the past participle of the main verb. It is used to express an action that happened before another past action. Example: 'Quando cheguei, ela já tinha saído' (When I arrived, she had already left). Regular past participles end in -ado (verbs ending in -ar) and -ido (verbs ending in -er/-ir). Some irregular past participles: feito (hacer), dito (decir), escrito (escribir), visto (ver), posto (poner), aberto (abrir), etc. In spoken language, it is common to use 'ter' instead of 'haver' (the latter being more formal). Unlike Spanish, where the past participle is invariable, in Portuguese it can agree with the direct object in constructions with 'ter' (e.g., 'Tinha escrito as cartas' or 'Tinha escritas as cartas' – although agreement is optional and more frequent in formal registers). The auxiliary 'haber' is not used in the standard compound form.

concept_examples.text: Quando cheguei, ela já tinha saído.
concept_examples.translation: When I arrived, she had already left.

concept_examples.text: Ele tinha estudado antes do exame.
concept_examples.translation: He had studied before the exam.

common_error.wrong: Quando cheguei, ela já tinha saída.
common_error.correct: Quando cheguei, ela já tinha saído.
common_error.explanation: The error occurs because in Spanish, with the auxiliary 'haber', the past participle is invariable ('había salido'). When transferring this to Portuguese, some students try to agree the past participle with the subject ('saída', feminine), but in the construction with 'ter' + past participle, the participle normally remains in the masculine singular (base form) when there is no explicit direct object. Only if there is a direct object can it optionally agree in some variants. For B1 level, it is recommended to always use the invariable form of the past participle in this compound tense.

levels.label: Formação e uso básico / Basic formation and use

examples.original: Eu tinha comido quando ela chegou.
examples.translation: I had eaten when she arrived.
examples.note: Shows the basic structure: tinha + regular past participle (-ido).

examples.original: Ela tinha falado comigo.
examples.translation: She had spoken to me.
examples.note: Regular past participle ending in -ado for -ar verbs.

examples.original: Nós tínhamos terminado o projeto.
examples.translation: We had finished the project.
examples.note: Optional agreement with the direct object: 'terminado' (invariable) or 'terminados' (if referring to 'projeto' – but in European Portuguese the invariable form is more common).

examples.original: Ele tinha escrito uma carta.
examples.translation: He had written a letter.

examples.original: Nós tínhamos feito os exercícios.
examples.translation: We had done the exercises.

examples.original: Ela tinha aberto a janela.
examples.translation: She had opened the window.

levels.label: Uso com ações sequenciais / Use with sequential actions

examples.original: Depois que ele tinha saído, começou a chover.
examples.phonetic: /deˈpɔjs ki ˈe.li ˈtĩ.ɲɐ saˈi.du, ko.meˈsow a ʃoˈveʁ/
examples.translation: After he had left, it started to rain.
examples.note: The pluperfect indicates the earlier action; the second action is in simple past.

examples.original: Ela percebeu que tinha esquecido as chaves.
examples.phonetic: /ˈɛ.lɐ peʁ.seˈbew ki ˈtĩ.ɲɐ ʃkeˈsi.du as ˈʃa.vis/
examples.translation: She realized she had forgotten the keys.
examples.note: Use with perception verbs; the pluperfect expresses the action prior to the realization.

examples.original: Quando chegaram, o filme já tinha começado.
examples.phonetic: /ˈkwɐ̃.du ʃeˈɡa.ɾɐ̃w, u ˈfiw.mi ʒa ˈtĩ.ɲɐ ko.meˈsa.du/
examples.translation: When they arrived, the movie had already started.
examples.note: Typical use to describe a situation already in progress.

title: Condicionais Tipo 1 e 2 / Type 1 and 2 Conditionals
bridge: In Spanish you use 'si + present + future' for real conditions (type 1) and 'si + imperfect subjunctive + conditional' for hypothetical ones (type 2). In Portuguese, the structure is similar, but there are traps: for type 2, the verb in the condition is in the 'imperfeito do subjuntivo' (which matches Spanish), but the result is formed with 'iria/iríamos' or 'faria/faríamos' (equivalent to the conditional). Be careful: in Portuguese you do NOT use the subjunctive after 'se' in type 1 (you use the present indicative, just like in Spanish, but don’t confuse it with the future subjunctive which is rarely used anymore). Also, the conditional 'se' is pronounced 'si', but it is written 'se'.
rule:
In Portuguese, conditionals are formed as follows:
- Type 1 (real): 'se' + present indicative + future of the present (or present, or imperative). Examples: 'Se eu puder, vou' (If I can, I will) – although here we use the future subjunctive, which in colloquial speech is replaced by the present indicative: 'Se eu posso, vou'. For B1 level, we use: 'Se fizeres isso, ficarei contente' (If you do that, I will be happy) – but in Brazil it is said 'Se você fizer isso, ficarei contente'. More common: 'Se você estudar, passará' (If you study, you will pass).
- Type 2 (unreal): 'se' + imperfect subjunctive + future of the past (conditional). Example: 'Se eu tivesse dinheiro, compraria uma casa' (If I had money, I would buy a house).
Exceptions and uses: In type 2, the imperfect subjunctive is formed regularly: -r (falasse, comesse, partisse). The conditional is formed with the infinitive + -ia, -ias, -ia, -íamos, -íeis, -iam. For irregular verbs: ser (seria), ter (teria), fazer (faria), dizer (diria). In type 1, for future events the future of the present (falarei) or the periphrastic 'ir + infinitive' (vou falar) is used. In type 2, 'iria + infinitive' (iria comprar) can also be used instead of the conditional, especially in Brazil. Be careful: in Portuguese you do NOT use the present subjunctive after 'se' in real conditions, as was done in old Spanish ('si tengas' does not exist); the present indicative is used. For unlikely conditions, the imperfect subjunctive is used, which is equivalent to the Spanish imperfect subjunctive. In Portuguese, the future subjunctive (quando/se você falar) is used with 'quando' and 'se' for upcoming events, but in the protasis of type 1 it is normal.
Typical use: Times are often mixed in conversation, but for B1 it is correct to maintain the classic structure.

concept_examples.text: Se você estudar, passará no exame.
concept_examples.translation: If you study, you will pass the exam.
concept_examples.phonetic: si voˈse stuˈdaʁ paˈsaɾa nu eˈzami

concept_examples.text: Se eu tivesse tempo, viajaria mais.
concept_examples.translation: If I had time, I would travel more.
concept_examples.phonetic: si ew ʧiˈvɛsi ˈtẽpu vjaʒaˈɾiɐ ˈmajs

concept_examples.text: Se chover, não vamos à praia.
concept_examples.translation: If it rains, we are not going to the beach.
concept_examples.phonetic: si ʃoˈveɾ nɐ̃w ˈvɐ̃wz a ˈpɾajɐ

concept_examples.text: Se eu fosse rico, ajudaria os pobres.
concept_examples.translation: If I were rich, I would help the poor.
concept_examples.phonetic: si ew ˈfɔsi ˈxiku aʒudaˈɾiɐ us ˈpɔbɾis

common_error.wrong: Se eu seria rico, compraria um carro.
common_error.correct: Se eu fosse rico, compraria um carro.
common_error.correct_alt: Se eu fosse rico, iria comprar um carro.
common_error.explanation: In Spanish, people sometimes incorrectly say 'si sería' (instead of 'si fuera'), but in Portuguese this is a very common mistake among Spanish speakers because the form 'seria' (conditional) resembles the Spanish 'sería'. Remember: in the condition (protasis) of type 2, you always use the imperfect subjunctive (fosse, tivesse, etc.), never the conditional. To avoid this, think: 'se' is always followed by the subjunctive (in type 2), not by the conditional.

levels.label: Variações e combinações com 'quando' e verbos modais
levels.translation: Variations and combinations with 'when' and modal verbs

examples.original: Se puder, quero falar com você amanhã.
examples.phonetic: si puˈdeɾ ˈkɛɾu faˈlaʁ kõ voˈse ɐmɐˈɲɐ̃
examples.translation: If I can, I want to talk to you tomorrow.

examples.original: Quando eu tiver tempo, vou fazer exercício.
examples.phonetic: ˈkwɐ̃du ew ʧiˈveʁ ˈtẽpu vow faˈzeɾ ezeʁˈsisiu
examples.translation: When I have time, I am going to do exercise.

examples.original: Se ela quisesse, poderia vir conosco.
examples.phonetic: si ˈɛla kiˈzɛsi poˈdeɾiɐ viʁ koˈnɔsku
examples.translation: If she wanted to, she could come with us.

title: Voz Passiva / Passive Voice (present and past)
bridge: In Spanish, the passive voice is formed with 'ser' + past participle (e.g., 'la carta es escrita'). In Portuguese, the structure is almost identical: 'ser' + past participle, but there are important differences in the conjugation of the participle (which in Portuguese always agrees in gender and number) and in the use of the auxiliary 'ser' or 'estar' depending on the nuance of action or state. Additionally, in Portuguese, the agent complement is usually introduced with 'por' (or 'pela', 'pelos', etc.), not with 'de' as is sometimes done in Spanish. Be careful: in the passive voice, the participle in Portuguese does not vary when 'ser' is used with compound tenses, but it does agree in simple forms. Also note that in Portuguese, the passive voice with 'se' (partícula apassivadora) is used much more frequently than in Spanish.
rule: The passive voice in Portuguese is formed with the auxiliary verb SER or ESTAR (more frequently SER) in any tense + the past participle of the main verb. The participle agrees in gender and number with the patient subject: 'A carta é escrita', 'As cartas são escritas'. In the simple present: 'eu sou', 'tu és', 'ele/ela é', 'nós somos', 'vós sois' (archaic, 'vocês são' is used), 'eles/elas são'. In the past (simple or compound perfect preterite): 'eu fui', 'tu foste', 'ele/ela foi', 'nós fomos', 'vós fostes', 'eles/elas foram'. For the compound perfect preterite, 'tem sido' + participle is used (e.g., 'tem sido escrito'). The agent complement is introduced with the preposition 'por' (with contractions: pelo(s), pela(s)): 'A carta foi escrita pela Maria'. There is also the passive voice with 'se' (pronominal passive), which is very frequently used in Portuguese: 'Vendem-se casas' (houses are sold), where the verb agrees with the patient subject. Exception: verbs that use both irregular and regular participles indistinctly (like 'imprimir' - impresso/imprimido), but in the passive voice the irregular participle is preferred. In the past, it is common to use 'foi' + participle for punctual actions and 'era' + participle for descriptions or habitual actions in the past. Note that in Portuguese, unlike Spanish, 'ser' + participle is not used to form the passive of permanent states (this is done with 'estar' + participle, indicating a result). At B1 level, focus on mastering the passive with SER in the present and simple past mainly.

concept_examples.text: A casa é construída pelos trabalhadores.
concept_examples.translation: The house is built by the workers.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɐ ˈkazɐ ɛ kõʃtɾuˈidɐ ˈpeʎuʃ tɾɐbɐʎɐˈdoɾiʃ/ (European Portuguese)

concept_examples.text: O bolo foi comido pela criança.
concept_examples.translation: The cake was eaten by the child.
concept_examples.phonetic: /u ˈbolu foj kuˈmidu ˈpɛlɐ kɾiˈɐ̃sɐ/ (Brazilian Portuguese)

concept_examples.text: As cartas são enviadas todas as semanas.
concept_examples.translation: The letters are sent every week.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɐʃ ˈkaɾtɐʃ sɐ̃ũ ẽviˈadɐʃ ˈtɔdɐʃ ɐʃ sɨˈmɐnɐʃ/ (European Portuguese)

concept_examples.text: A notícia foi publicada no jornal.
concept_examples.translation: The news was published in the newspaper.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɐ nuˈtisjɐ foj publikaˈdɐ nu ʒuɾˈnaʊ/ (Brazilian Portuguese)

common_error.wrong: A casa foi construída de os trabalhadores.
common_error.correct: A casa foi construída pelos trabalhadores.
common_error.correct_alt: A casa foi construída por os trabalhadores. (less common, but acceptable in informal register)
common_error.explanation: The error is using the preposition 'de' to introduce the agent, as is sometimes done in Spanish with 'de' in passive constructions with participles of Latin origin (e.g., 'una obra de Picasso'). In Portuguese, the agent complement is always introduced with 'por', which contracts with definite articles: pelo(s), pela(s). Using 'de' will result in an incorrect phrase or one with a different meaning. Remember: always use 'por' + agent.

examples.original: O pão é feito pela padaria.
examples.translation: The bread is made by the bakery.
examples.note: Agreement: 'pão' (masculine singular) → 'feito'. The preposition 'pela' is a contraction of 'por + a'.

examples.original: As portas são abertas às oito horas.
examples.phonetic: /ɐʃ ˈpɔɾtɐʃ sɐ̃ũ ɐˈbɛɾtɐʃ az ˈojtu ˈɔɾɐʃ/ (European)
examples.translation: The doors are opened at eight o'clock.
examples.note: 'Portas' feminine plural → 'abertas' agrees in feminine plural.

examples.original: Este livro é lido por muitos estudantes.
examples.phonetic: /ˈeʃtʃi ˈlivɾu ɛ ˈlidu puɾ ˈmũjtuʃ ʃtudaˈdʒiʃ/ (Brazilian)
examples.translation: This book is read by many students.
examples.note: The agent 'muitos estudantes' does not take a contraction with an article, so 'por' without contraction is used.

levels.label: Voz Passiva no Passado (Pretérito Perfeito)
levels.translation: Passive voice in the past (simple perfect preterite)

examples.original: O filme foi dirigido por um diretor famoso.
examples.phonetic: /u ˈfiwmi foj dʒiɾiˈʒidu puɾ ũ dʒiɾeˈtoɾ fɐˈmozu/ (Brazilian)
examples.translation: The movie was directed by a famous director.
examples.note: In Portuguese, 'dirigido' remains invariable in gender because the subject is masculine singular. If it were 'A filme' (not common), we would say 'dirigida'.

examples.original: As cidades foram destruídas pelo terremoto.
examples.translation: The cities were destroyed by the earthquake.
examples.note: The auxiliary 'foram' (3rd person plural) and participle 'destruídas' agree with 'cidades' (feminine plural).

examples.original: A carta foi escrita à mão.
examples.translation: The letter was written by hand.
examples.note: When there is no explicit agent, only the participle and auxiliary are used.

levels.label: Passiva com 'se' e diferenças com o espanhol
levels.translation: Passive with 'se' and differences with Spanish

examples.original: Vendem-se casas nesta região.
examples.translation: Houses are sold in this region.
examples.note: In Portuguese, the verb agrees with the patient subject: 'casas' (plural) → 'vendem'. Do not say 'vende-se casas'.

examples.original: Fala-se português no Brasil.
examples.translation: Portuguese is spoken in Brazil.
examples.note: With a singular subject, the verb is singular. 'Fala-se' is equivalent to 'se habla'.

examples.original: As inscrições fazem-se até sexta-feira.
examples.phonetic: /ɐʃ ʃĩskɾiˈsõis ˈfazẽj si ɐˈtɛ ˈseʃtɐ ˈfejɾɐ/ (Brazilian)
examples.translation: Registrations are made until Friday.
examples.note: The pronoun 'se' can appear after the verb and with a postponed subject. Agreement is mandatory.
